children: Cattle futures are higher after the USDA on Friday reported the lowest placements on feedlots for August on records stretching back to 1996. The 1.62 million head placed in August were 9% below the year-earlier month. Marketings of fed cattle at 1.52 million head were down3% on the year and also a record low for August. Cattle and calves on feed as of Sept. 1 stood at 11.2 million head, up 1% from a year earlier. "As weather cools, more cattle should be placed and marketing should increase," Chris Lehner of ADM Investor Services says in a note. Imported Mexican cattle should also start to show up in placements, he adds. Live cattle are up 1.7% on CME. Lean hogs rise 1.5%. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
